commits.message:
feat: implement signature_verification_in_loop lint

Flag env.crypto().ed25519_verify(...), secp256k1_recover(...), and
secp256r1_verify(...) calls made inside a loop body. Elliptic-curve
signature verification is one of the most CPU-expensive host functions
available, and unlike a host call with a constant result, this cost
cannot be hoisted out of the loop: each iteration verifies a different
signature. Verifying signatures one at a time in a loop is a structural
sign that the contract should use a scheme that supports batch or
aggregate verification, or move per-item auth to a bulk callee
entrypoint.

- Add SignatureVerificationInLoop late lint pass matching the three
  Crypto/CryptoHazmat signature-verification and key-recovery methods,
  unconditionally flagged inside a loop (no loop-invariance check, since
  the cost is inherent to what the loop is doing, matching the existing
  contract_call_in_loop lint's approach).
- Add UI fixtures covering all three methods across for/while/loop forms,
  a call outside a loop, and an #[allow] suppression case.
- Document the lint in docs/lints/signature_verification_in_loop.md, the
  README feature list, docs/lints/README.md, docs/cost_rationale.md, and
  CHANGELOG.md, including why Address::require_auth() and BLS/BN254
  pairing checks are deliberately out of scope for this first pass.

Closes #47

Merge remote-tracking branch 'upstream/main' into feat/signature-verification-in-loop

# Conflicts:
#	soroban_cost_lints/ui/main.stderr

fix: resolve CI build failures in SARIF output and fixture workspace

- SarifRun.results was typed Vec<SarifResult> while the SARIF result
  builder constructed plain serde_json::Value objects via json!(),
  a leftover mismatch from a prior merge that broke compilation.
  Retype results as Vec<serde_json::Value>, drop the now-dead typed
  Sarif* structs, and wire the already-collected rule descriptors
  into tool.driver.rules.
- integration.rs used HashSet<String> but inserted &str literals;
  fix the declared type.
- alpha/beta fixture crates each declared their own [workspace]
  while also being listed as members of the parent workspace,
  causing cargo metadata to fail with "multiple workspace roots
  found". Drop the redundant per-crate [workspace] tables.

These were the actual cause of the "SARIF result missing level"
CI failures reported on PRs #232, #267, #269, #270 (all inherited
the same broken merge state) — the binary failed to compile, it
was not a runtime field-mapping bug.
